name: Titan-X
description: Engineered for maximum scientific payload and endurance. The Titan-X features reinforced structural spars and high-capacity fuel manifolds, but its immense mass requires heavy-lift launch vehicles and limits maneuverability.
specialAbility: Heavy Cargo Bay: +25% fuel tank volume & +10% payload mass allowance
disadvantage: High Dry Mass: Requires heavy launch vehicle tier & higher delta-V burns

name: Aero-Dart
description: Constructed from carbon-composite microlattices, the Aero-Dart is designed for rapid transit and flybys. Due to its lightweight minimalist frame, it has strictly 3 modification hardpoints and lower hull resilience.
specialAbility: High Delta-V Efficiency: +15% effective thruster Isp due to low inertia
disadvantage: Structural Fragility: Only 3 hardpoint slots and vulnerability to micrometeorites

name: Nova-Core
description: NASA's premier balanced architecture. Equipped with an experimental magnetoplasmadynamic propulsion harness and integrated optical communication bus. Offers reliable operational flexibility across all mission profiles.
specialAbility: Hybrid Power Grid: Solar and RTG power distribution efficiency +12%
disadvantage: Experimental Avionics: Slight budget premium and complex component tolerances

name: Goliath
description: A fortress against lethal radiation belts and particle fields. Built with tungsten-boron composite shielding and triple-redundant structural bulkheads. However, heavy shielding attenuates antenna gain, reducing effective comm range.
specialAbility: Aegis Bulkhead: Natural 35% radiation attenuation and double micrometeorite resistance
disadvantage: Comm Attenuation: Weak default high-gain array, requires dedicated comm upgrades
